question: Which of the following items is a source of light?
options: A lit campfire
A shiny glass mirror
The Moon at night
A polished metal tray
answer: A lit campfire

question: How can a student see a wooden pencil lying on his desk during the daytime?
options: Light from the window reflects off the pencil into his eyes
The pencil produces its own light which enters his eyes
His eyes send out light rays to shine on the pencil
Light bends around his eyes to reach the pencil
answer: Light from the window reflects off the pencil into his eyes

question: Siti tried to look at a light bulb through a flexible rubber hose that was bent into an S-shape. Why could she NOT see the light?
options: Light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through a bent hose
Rubber absorbs all light rays completely
Light turns into heat inside bent hoses
The light bulb stops glowing when viewed through rubber
answer: Light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through a bent hose

question: Why is a dark shadow formed on a wall when an opaque wooden toy is held in front of a torch?
options: The wooden toy blocks light because light travels in straight lines
The torch pulls dark air toward the wooden toy
Light bends around the toy to leave a dark spot in the center
The wooden toy absorbs all the room temperature
answer: The wooden toy blocks light because light travels in straight lines

question: Which material allows ALL or MOST light to pass through it, casting almost no shadow?
options: Clear glass pane
Tracing paper sheet
Thick cardboard box
Aluminium foil sheet
answer: Clear glass pane

question: John wants to make the shadow of a tennis ball on a screen LARGER. What should he do?
options: Move the torch closer to the tennis ball
Move the tennis ball closer to the screen
Move the torch further away from the tennis ball
Move both the torch and screen further away
answer: Move the torch closer to the tennis ball

question: At what time of day will a tree outdoors cast its SHORTEST shadow on the grass?
options: 12:00 noon
answer: 12:00 noon

question: An opaque cardboard sheet with a small square hole in the middle is placed between a torch and a screen. What will appear on the screen?
options: A dark rectangular shadow with a bright square in the middle
A bright square background with a dark card shadow
A completely dark shadow with no light passing through
A bright circle with a dark square in the middle
answer: A dark rectangular shadow with a bright square in the middle

question: Which statement correctly describes how light behaves when it hits a flat mirror?
options: Light reflects off the smooth mirror surface in a straight line
Light passes straight through the mirror without stopping
Light is absorbed completely by the mirror and turned into heat
Light bends around the mirror edges to create a dark shadow
answer: Light reflects off the smooth mirror surface in a straight line

question: A student enters a room with no light sources and all windows covered. Why can she NOT see her white shoes?
options: There is no light source to reflect off her shoes into her eyes
White shoes stop reflecting light when it is quiet
Human eyes can only see objects that generate heat
Her shoes absorb all darkness and become transparent
answer: There is no light source to reflect off her shoes into her eyes

question: In a shadow experiment, keeping the torch and object fixed while moving the screen CLOSER to the object will make the shadow:
options: Smaller
Larger
Stay the exact same size
Disappear completely
answer: Smaller

question: A periscope allows a child to see over a high wall using two flat mirrors. How does light reach the child's eyes?
options: Light reflects off the top mirror, then off the bottom mirror into the eyes
Light travels straight through both mirrors without bouncing
Light from the eyes shines through the mirrors to illuminate the wall
Light bends continuously inside the tube without touching any mirrors
answer: Light reflects off the top mirror, then off the bottom mirror into the eyes

question: Which of the following is a main natural source of heat for Earth?
options: The Sun
An electric toaster
A glass mirror
The ocean
answer: The Sun

question: What is the definition of the temperature of an object?
options: A measurement of its degree of hotness
The total amount of heat energy stored inside it
The time it takes for an object to freeze
The weight and size of the object
answer: A measurement of its degree of hotness

question: Which statement correctly distinguishes heat from temperature?
options: Heat is a form of energy, while temperature measures degree of hotness
Heat is measured in degree Celsius, while temperature is measured in units of energy
Temperature flows from hot to cold, while heat remains stationary
Temperature rises when heat is lost, while heat rises when temperature drops
answer: Heat is a form of energy, while temperature measures degree of hotness

question: A hot iron spoon at 80°C is dipped into a bowl of cold soup at 15°C. What is the direction of heat flow?
options: From the hot spoon to the cold soup
From the cold soup to the hot spoon
Heat flows back and forth equally between both
No heat flows because one is solid and one is liquid
answer: From the hot spoon to the cold soup

question: Heat will continue to flow between two touching metal keys until:
options: Both keys reach the exact same temperature
One key reaches 0°C and the other reaches 100°C
All heat energy in both keys is completely lost
The smaller key absorbs all the heat from the larger key
answer: Both keys reach the exact same temperature

question: What happens to the temperature of a glass of room-temperature water when it GAINS heat?
options: Its temperature increases
Its temperature decreases
Its temperature drops to 0°C
Its temperature stays unchanged
answer: Its temperature increases

question: What happens to the temperature of a warm metal plate when it LOSES heat to the air?
options: Its temperature decreases
Its temperature increases
Its temperature remains constant
Its temperature drops immediately to 0°C
answer: Its temperature decreases

question: When reading the temperature on a glass liquid thermometer, how should a student align his eyes?
options: Level with the top of the liquid column
Looking down from above the top of the stem
Looking up from below the glass bulb
At any convenient side angle
answer: Level with the top of the liquid column

question: Why does the liquid inside a glass thermometer rise when placed in hot water?
options: The liquid gains heat from the hot water and expands
The liquid loses heat to the hot water and contracts
The glass tube squeezes tight to push the liquid up
Air enters the bulb and pushes the liquid upward
answer: The liquid gains heat from the hot water and expands

question: Beaker A has 400 ml of water at 70°C. Beaker B has 100 ml of water at 70°C. Which statement is correct?
options: Both beakers have the same temperature, but Beaker A has more heat energy
Beaker A has a higher temperature than Beaker B
Beaker B contains more heat energy because it has less water
Both beakers contain the exact same amount of heat energy
answer: Both beakers have the same temperature, but Beaker A has more heat energy

question: When a student holds an ice cube in her hand, her hand feels cold. Why?
options: Her hand loses heat to the colder ice cube
Coldness leaves the ice cube and enters her hand
Her hand gains temperature from the ice cube
The ice cube loses heat to the surrounding air only
answer: Her hand loses heat to the colder ice cube
